index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a schematic comparison of two types of multilayer networks, labeled (a) and (b), under the overarching title 'Multilayer Networks'. The layout is divided into two side-by-side panels, each illustrating a distinct network structure within a parallelogram-shaped plane representing a layer or set of layers.

In panel (a), titled 'Without Interlayer', a single layer is depicted containing six purple circular nodes arranged horizontally. These nodes are connected by two types of intra-layer edges: solid green curved lines and dashed red curved lines. These represent two independent connection types within the same layer, such as different transportation modes in a city. The green and red edges form overlapping connections between nodes, indicating multiple interaction types coexisting within one layer. There are no vertical or inter-layer connections shown, emphasizing the absence of coupling between layers.

Panel (b), titled 'With Interlayer', illustrates a two-layer multilayer network. Each layer contains five blue circular nodes arranged horizontally, with the top layer positioned above the bottom layer. Within each layer, nodes are connected by solid black straight lines, representing intra-layer interactions (e.g., social interactions on separate platforms like LinkedIn and Twitter). Additionally, vertical dashed black lines connect corresponding nodes across the two layers, symbolizing inter-layer connections. These dashed lines indicate that identical nodes exist in both layers and are linked, forming a coupled multilayer structure. The intra-layer connections are encoded in Laplacian matrices L^(1) and L^(2), while the inter-layer connections are encoded in the Laplacian matrix B, as referenced in Equation (\ref{intralayer_lsup_lap_mlil}).

The visual distinction between the two panels lies in the presence or absence of vertical dashed lines connecting nodes across layers. Panel (a) emphasizes intra-layer diversity without inter-layer coupling, whereas panel (b) demonstrates both intra-layer and inter-layer connectivity, forming a fully coupled multilayer network. The color coding—purple for panel (a) and blue for panel (b)—helps differentiate the two scenarios. All connections are drawn with consistent line styles: solid for intra-layer and dashed for inter-layer (in panel b), ensuring clarity in distinguishing interaction types.
